title: NIR: Neuromorphic Intermediate Representation reference implementation
summary: The NIR project provides a computational intermediate representation enabling interoperability across neuromorphic frameworks and hardware. Supported by nine simulators and five platforms as of July 2023, it allows model portability between tools like Lava-DL, Nengo, and SpiNNaker2 via save/load operations. An extension named NIRData facilitates data exchange for spiking neural networks. The software was conceived at the Telluride Neuromorphic Workshop in September 2023 and published as a Nature Communications article in September 2024.
tldr: NIR is an open-source intermediate representation enabling model portability across multiple neuromorphic simulators and hardware platforms, with support for spiking neural network data exchange via NIRData.
evidence: NIR is a set of computational primitives, shared across different neuromorphic frameworks and technology stacks.
NIR is currently supported by 9 simulators and 5 hardware platforms
Using NIR is typically a part of your favorite framework's workflow
